newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Daimler-Benz said agreeing to Ssangyong stake hike.
newsitem.headline: Daimler-Benz said agreeing to Ssangyong stake hike.

text.p: Ssangyong Motor and partner Daimler-Benz AG have tentatively agreed that the German firm would raise its stake in Ssangyong to 45 percent or more, a senior Ssangyong financial manager said on Thursday.
Confirmation from Daimler-Benz, which now has a 2.55 percent stake, was not available. And a Ssangyong Group spokesman denied any agreement had been reached.
"We expect the final agreement in mid-August or in September. The German company is now evaluating our assets," said the financial manager, who declined to be identified.

The domestic Chosun Ilbo newspaper said Ssangyong and Daimler-Benz had tentatively agreed on the capital injection as the German partner expected strong sales of Ssangyong's new model sedan "Chairman".
Ssangyong Motor has suffered from huge losses, a result of massive investments in new models.
Ssangyong's debts are currently estimated at 3.2 trillion won. The nation's four-wheel-drive utility vehicle maker incurred losses of 228.5 billion won in 1996 on sales of 1.37 trillion won in 1995.
